title: Mesh Analysis: KVL Loop by Loop
topic: Mesh analysis — assign a clockwise current to every independent loop, write KVL around each, and solve the resulting linear system. The shared branch between two adjacent loops carries the difference of the two mesh currents.

beats.narration: Two loops sharing a wire — how do we find the current through the middle branch?

elements.content: Manimo enters centre-screen
Two loops, one shared wire — what flows in the middle?

beats.narration: Here's a two-mesh circuit. A battery on the left, another on the right, and a resistor in the middle shared between both loops.

elements.content: Outer rectangle with shared vertical middle branch (two adjacent loops)
Battery V1 in left mesh
Resistor R1 in left mesh top
Shared resistor R3 in middle branch
Resistor R2 in right mesh top
Battery V2 in right mesh
Labels: V1=12V, R1=4Ω, R3=6Ω, R2=2Ω, V2=6V

beats.narration: Assign a clockwise current to each loop — I one in the left mesh, I two in the right. Both currents pass through the shared resistor — but in opposite directions.

elements.content: Rotating arrows showing I1 clockwise around left mesh
Rotating arrows showing I2 clockwise around right mesh
I1 label inside left mesh
I2 label inside right mesh
in the middle branch the net current is I1 − I2

beats.narration: Write KVL around each loop. Left loop: V one equals I one R one plus I one minus I two times R three. Right loop: minus V two equals I two R two plus I two minus I one times R three.

elements.content: Left mesh: V₁ = I₁R₁ + (I₁ − I₂)R₃
Right mesh: −V₂ = I₂R₂ + (I₂ − I₁)R₃
two linear equations in two unknowns
Solve: I₁ ≈ 1.5 A, I₂ ≈ 0 A

beats.narration: One mesh current per loop, KVL applied loop by loop — that's mesh analysis. For n loops you get n equations and n unknowns.

elements.content: One mesh current per loop. KVL each loop. Solve.
n loops → n equations, n unknowns
